Section 1: Executive Summary & Operating Reality

Yelp Inc. (NYSE: YELP) operates a leading local directory and high-intent local services marketplace, currently led by Co-Founder and active Chief Executive Officer Jeremy Stoppelman alongside Chief Financial Officer David Schwarzbach and Chief Operating Officer Jed Nachman. In its second quarter 2026 financial report (ended June 30, 2026), Yelp reported GAAP net revenue of $375.5 million, up 1.4% year-over-year. Top-line growth was sustained by non-advertising "Other Revenue"—which nearly doubled (+98% YoY to $33.0 million) due to the acquisition of AI lead management platform Hatch, rapid adoption of the Yelp Host call-answering SaaS product, and multi-year data licensing partnerships with OpenAI and enterprise AI developers. However, core advertising revenue contracted 3% YoY to $342.5 million as persistent macroeconomic pressure squeezed small and medium-sized business (SMB) promotional budgets, particularly within Restaurants, Retail & Other (RR&O) categories (-10% YoY).

Operating profitability faced near-term margin compression during Q2 2026. GAAP Operating Income (EBIT) stood at $43.7 million, representing an 11.6% operating margin compared to 14.4% in the prior-year period (-280 bps YoY). This contraction stemmed from increased website infrastructure overhead required to power AI tools, higher capitalized software depreciation, and expanded sales headcount for Hatch. GAAP Net Income fell 28% YoY to $31.7 million ($0.57 diluted EPS), while Adjusted EBITDA came in at $91.4 million (24.3% margin). Operating cash flow remained resilient at $75.8 million, yielding $61.1 million in Free Cash Flow. Management narrowed full-year 2026 guidance, projecting net revenue between $1.460 billion and $1.470 billion and Adjusted EBITDA between $315 million and $325 million. Importantly, Yelp has temporarily paused its share repurchase program to prioritize paying down $100.0 million drawn on its revolving credit facility to fund the $271.2 million cash purchase of Hatch, planning to resume repurchases in 2027.

C-Suite Strategic & Capital Allocation Insights (Q2 2026 Earnings Call):

"Yelp's AI transformation continued to gain momentum in the second quarter, with encouraging signs across several key metrics and Other revenue nearly doubling year over year... Yelp Assistant drove early positive signs in engagement, Yelp Host scaled rapidly, and Hatch accelerated their product roadmap. At the same time, our trusted content is powering local discovery for ChatGPT and other AI partners."
— Jeremy Stoppelman, Co-Founder & CEO

"First quarter net revenue of $376 million and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 24% both exceeded the high end of our outlook... While local economies remained pressured, Other revenue accelerated to a record $33 million. We are continuing to invest in our strategic initiatives while pausing share repurchases to pay down our revolving credit facility following the Hatch acquisition, with plans to resume repurchases in 2027."
— David Schwarzbach, CFO

Section 2: Business Model Reality, Unit Economics & Competitive Moat

Yelp monetizes commercial intent at the point of local discovery. The business model has strategically shifted away from low-margin restaurant and retail ad placements toward high-value Home & Local Services (plumbing, HVAC, legal, roofing, auto care). Advertisers purchase cost-per-click (CPC) ads, sponsored search placements, and project lead generation products through "Request-a-Quote" workflows. Additionally, Yelp generates recurring SaaS subscription fees from business tools (Yelp Host AI phone reservation and call handling, Hatch AI lead conversion) and collects multi-year licensing fees by providing clean, human-generated review data to AI models like OpenAI's ChatGPT.

Switching Costs & Evidence of Pricing Power: Yelp’s moat relies on a two-sided network effect built on over 330 million cumulative reviews and 510,000 active paying advertising locations. For local service professionals, shifting away from Yelp carries high customer acquisition switching costs; Yelp leads exhibit high commercial intent compared to passive social media impressions. Pricing power is evident in unit pricing dynamics: despite a 5% YoY decline in ad clicks during Q2 2026, average cost-per-click (CPC) increased by 1% YoY, demonstrating that local merchants are willing to pay premium rates for verified, conversion-ready customer leads.

Structural Secular Tailwinds vs. Competitive Disruption Risks:

  • Secular Tailwinds: The rapid digitization of home services provides a structural expansion runway for Yelp’s highest-margin category (Services represent 64% of ad revenue). Furthermore, generative AI platforms require reliable, real-time local business metadata and authentic human opinions. Yelp’s multi-year licensing deals (e.g., OpenAI partnership) monetize its 330M+ review database as high-margin data licensing float. Proprietary AI tools like Yelp Assistant (+10% project submission lift) and Yelp Host (2.4M automated call run-rate) enhance merchant productivity and create sticky recurring SaaS revenue.
  • Competitive Disruption & Substitution Threats: Google Search remains Yelp's dominant top-of-funnel discovery bottleneck. The rollout of Google AI Overviews (SGE) risks cannibalizing organic referral traffic by answering user local queries directly on Google search results pages without directing users to external sites. Furthermore, SMB ad budgets are highly sensitive to macro slowdowns, as evidenced by the 10% YoY revenue decline in RR&O categories during Q2 2026.

Section 3: Forensic Cash Flow, SBC Dilution & Owner Earnings Audit

A rigorous audit of Yelp Inc. (YELP) requires looking past management's preferred Non-GAAP metric—Adjusted EBITDA ($369.2 million in FY 2025)—which routinely adds back real economic operating expenses, most notably Stock-Based Compensation (SBC) and property/software maintenance capital expenditures. Treating stock-based compensation as a non-cash item creates a massive distortion in reported profitability: while SBC does not require immediate cash disbursement, it represents direct economic equity dilution that transfers enterprise value from public shareholders to employees.

Forensic Cash Flow Insight: Management promoted an Adjusted EBITDA of $369.2M in FY 2025 and guided to $315M–$325M for FY 2026. However, after deducting 100% of SBC ($131.2M in FY 2025) and required Maintenance CapEx ($48.4M), true Buffett Owner Earnings were $192.4M in FY 2025 and $184.5M on a TTM run-rate basis. While Yelp has structurally reduced SBC as a percentage of revenue from ~12% in prior years down to 8%–9% by late 2025, SBC remains an unavoidable annual equity burden of $108M–$113M that must be deducted from operating cash flows.

Float & Interest Rate Sensitivity Audit

Because Yelp's unearned customer deferred revenue ($11.6 million) represents less than 3.5% of annual operating cash flow and less than 7% of annual pre-tax operating income, the enterprise does not hold material customer float or escrow balances (unlike payroll processors or insurance carriers). Therefore, central bank interest rate decisions have zero direct operational impact on customer float earnings.

However, interest rate cycles impact Yelp's corporate balance sheet yield on its cash reserves and borrowing costs on its drawn revolving credit facility ($100 million at ~6.5% interest rate):

  • +100 bps Interest Rate Hike: Adds ~$0.94M in interest income on $94.1M cash reserves, offset by ($1.00M) in additional annual interest expense on the $100M drawn credit facility. Net Pre-Tax Owner Earnings Impact: -$0.06M (Negligible).
  • -100 bps Interest Rate Cut: Reduces interest expense on the credit facility by +$1.00M, offset by ($0.94M) lower yields on corporate cash deposits. Net Pre-Tax Owner Earnings Impact: +$0.06M (Negligible).

Section 4: Balance Sheet Fortress, Debt Leases & Ownership Check

Yelp's capital structure underwent a material pivot in early 2026. After operating with a debt-free, cash-rich balance sheet throughout 2024 and 2025, Yelp executed a major strategic acquisition of Hatch for $271.2 million in cash in February 2026, supplemented by $174 million in first-half 2026 share buybacks. To fund these capital expenditures, Yelp drew $100 million on its revolving credit facility, shifting its liquid fortress into a mild Net Debt position.

Furthermore, management explicitly announced in August 2026 that it has paused all share repurchases for the second half of 2026 and FY 2027 to allocate 100% of organic cash flow toward paying off the $100M facility.

However, the true net compounding impact must be adjusted for stock issued to employees via equity grants and net share tax settlements.

Section 5: Warren Buffett Owner Earnings Intrinsic Valuation Matrix

To evaluate Yelp Inc. (YELP) through the lens of Warren Buffett's 1986 Owner Earnings framework, we strip away promotional Non-GAAP metrics such as Adjusted EBITDA ($315M–$325M guidance) and unadjusted Free Cash Flow ($283.7M TTM). Non-GAAP EBITDA excludes stock-based compensation (SBC), which represents a real, non-negotiable economic cost to shareholders that dilutes equity.

Buffett Owner Earnings Derivation (Trailing Twelve Months):
  • GAAP Operating Cash Flow: $349.6M
  • Less: Maintenance Capital Expenditures (Software, servers, hosting): -$45.0M
  • Less: 100% Stock-Based Compensation (SBC): -$118.0M
  • Normalized Owner Earnings (Year 1): $186.6M (~$190.0M Normalized / $3.50 per share)

    • Yelp generates an exceptional 15.2% Owner Earnings Yield relative to its $1.25B market capitalization ($23.07 stock price across 54.26M diluted shares). However, capital allocation dynamics shifted significantly in 2026 following the $270M cash acquisition of Hatch. Management drew $100M on its revolving credit facility, turning Yelp's balance sheet into a net debt position of -$29.2M (-$0.55 per share). Consequently, aggressive share repurchases ($292M repurchased in 2025) have been temporarily paused to prioritize credit facility debt repayment, creating a short-term capital allocation pause before buybacks resume in 2027.

    Discount Rate Derivation: In accordance with Local Sovereign Hurdle Principles, the discount rate is anchored to the 10-Year US Treasury yield (~4.20%) plus a market equity risk premium (ERP) adjusted for Yelp's small-cap profile and search disintermediation risks:

    • Base Case Discount Rate: 4.20% US 10Y + 4.60% ERP = 8.80%
    • Bear Case Discount Rate: 4.20% US 10Y + 5.30% ERP (Elevated AI threat premium) = 9.50%
    • Bull Case Discount Rate: 4.20% US 10Y + 4.30% ERP = 8.50%

    Market-Implied Expectations & "What is Priced In?" (Reverse DCF)

    Inverting the valuation model at today's price of $23.07 reveals that Mr. Market is pricing in a 5-year Owner Earnings CAGR ($g_{\text{implied}}$) of -5.8% per year (assuming an 8.8% discount rate and 2.0% terminal growth).

    Analytical Conclusion: Market sentiment reflects extreme pessimism, assuming that generative AI search engines (Google AI Overviews, OpenAI ChatGPT) will permanently erode Yelp's local advertising monetization. While core Restaurant, Retail & Other (RR&O) advertising declined 10% YoY in Q2 2026, market pricing completely ignores Yelp's expansion into Home & Professional Services ($241M ad revenue), Hatch AI lead automation, and high-margin LLM data licensing agreements (including OpenAI).

    The 5-Year Market Closure Test

    If the New York Stock Exchange were to close for 5 years, an investor buying the entirety of Yelp today for $1.25B ($23.07 per share) would collect approximately $1.02B in cumulative organic Owner Cash Flows over 60 months (assuming Base Case cash generation of ~$190M–$220M/year). This represents an organic return of 81.6% of the purchase price in pure cash, independent of public equity market quotes or multiple expansion.

    3 Explicit Quantitative Pre-Mortem Falsification Triggers

    The investment thesis for Yelp Inc. shall be declared fundamentally broken and invalid if any of the following operational tripwires occur:

    1. Core Advertising Revenue Contraction: Combined Advertising Revenue (Services + RR&O) contracts by >6.0% YoY for two consecutive quarters, signaling structural market share loss to Google Local and vertical platforms.
    2. Stock-Based Compensation Expansion: Stock-Based Compensation exceeds 10.0% of total net revenue on a TTM basis, demonstrating management's inability to control executive dilution during a revenue slowdown.
    3. Paying Advertising Location Churn: Total Paying Advertising Locations fall below 475,000 locations (down from 510,000 in Q2 2026), indicating terminal merchant drop-off and defective ad ROI.
